title: Regimen: token SLO benchmarking and multi-region surge controller
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a reproducible benchmarking and telemetry pipeline ("Regimen") to validate token-level SLIs across model variants and quantization profiles, and implement a region-aware surge controller that adjusts admission thresholds during multi-region capacity events. This ticket covers the benchmark harness, Grafana dashboard buildout, failure-injection test plan, adaptive-shed controller prototype, and runbook for on-call engineers.
background_and_motivation: We frequently observe p99 token latency regressions during region surges and model rollouts. Existing dashboards show request-level latency but do not expose per-token behavior (kv-cache hit patterns, decode path hotspots) or the admission threshold decisions used by regional circuit-breakers. Teams need an observable baseline to tune SLOs and a controllable surge controller to safely shed load without global outages.
goals: Deliver a benchmark harness that measures per-token p50/p95/p99 across representative workloads (chat, long-form, embeddings) for selected model variants and quantization settings
Create a Grafana dashboard with: per-tenant token histograms, admission-score heatmap, regional admit rate, kv-cache hit-rate correlated with token latency, and cutover simulation panels
Prototype an adaptive multi-region surge controller that adjusts admission thresholds automatically based on golden signals and predicted capacity burn
Define a failure-injection plan (DNS drain, gradual capacity removal) and an on-call runbook for region cutovers and automated fallback to compact variants
Provide visible SLO acceptance criteria and an automated CI check that runs the Regimen benchmark on PRs affecting runtime admission or decode paths
work_breakdown: Bench: implement Regimen harness (python/locust wrapper + token-level instrumentation hooks) - marshalling seq-length cohorts and prompt archetypes
Telemetry: add per-token timing spans in runtime tracer (decode, kv lookup, attention kernels) and expose as metrics via otel/prometheus
Dashboard: Grafana buildout using new metrics; implement heatmap panels and cohort comparators
Controller: prototype adaptive surge controller service that subscribes to golden signals and surfaces suggested admission threshold changes
Testing: run failure-injection scenarios in staging (gradual region drain, model variant throttle), capture dashboards, iterate thresholds
Runbook: document escalation, manual override, and automated rollback steps; link PRs and dashboards
acceptance_criteria: Regimen harness can produce stable per-token p50/p95/p99 reports for at least 3 workload cohorts (chat-short, chat-long, embedding-bulk)
Grafana dashboard panels show token-latency histograms and admission-score heatmap; dashboard links included in ticket
Adaptive controller prototype recommends threshold adjustments and successfully triggers a safe, automated rollback to a compact model in staging during induced capacity pressure
Failure-injection runbook validated by executing 2 planned cutover drills in staging with on-call involvement
CI check created that runs a minimized Regimen run on PRs touching admission or decode code paths
risks_and_considerations: Per-token instrumentation adds overhead; need to validate sampling and low-overhead spans to avoid perturbing SLOs
Automated threshold changes could oscillate if signals are noisy; controller needs hysteresis and cooldown windows
Experimentation with fallback variants may expose model-regression risk; ensure evaluation harness and guardrails
Grafana panels need to scale as tenant cardinality grows; consider aggregation strategies and pre-aggregated histograms
